headline.title: AI is more likely than humans to form biases when hiring
headline.summary: New research indicates that AI systems, particularly large language models (LLMs), are more likely than humans to form biases during the hiring process, potentially affecting résumé screening. These biases can arise not only from the training data but also from the models' own learning processes.

articles.title: Cura 1T: Specialized Model for Agentic Healthcare
articles.summary: Cura 1T is a specialized language model designed for agentic healthcare applications, addressing high-stakes communication, expert reasoning, and workflow execution in medical settings. The model aims to integrate capabilities such as patient consultation, clinical reasoning, interactive diagnosis, and electronic health record management, overcoming limitations seen in existing healthcare AI models.

articles.title: Do Coding Agents Need Executable World Models, Simplification, and Verification to Solve ARC-AGI-3?
articles.summary: The article investigates the necessity of executable world models, simplification, and verification in enhancing the performance of coding agents in solving the ARC-AGI-3 challenge. It presents a study involving four Codex-based agents to determine the impact of these components on agent effectiveness.

articles.title: S1-Omni: A Unified Multimodal Reasoning Model for Scientific Understanding, Prediction, and Generation
articles.summary: S1-Omni is a new unified multimodal reasoning model designed to enhance scientific understanding, prediction, and generation by integrating various capabilities in AI for Science (AI4S). This model aims to overcome the limitations of fragmented approaches by consolidating heterogeneous data, scientific laws, and expert knowledge into a single framework.

articles.title: Partial Information Decomposition as a Multi-Contrast 3D MRI Selection Strategy for Resource-Constrained Deep Neural Network Training in Brain Tumor Segmentation
articles.summary: A study proposes a Partial Information Decomposition framework to optimize multi-contrast 3D MRI segmentation for brain tumor identification by selecting the most informative input pairs. The approach was tested using various MRI sequences and successfully identified T1c and T2-FLAIR as the most effective combination for training deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments.

articles.title: FLINT: Fingerprinting Federated Learning Architectures from 5G PHY-Layer Side Channels
articles.summary: Researchers have introduced FLINT, a method for fingerprinting federated learning architectures by exploiting side-channel information from 5G physical layer scheduling metadata. This approach addresses vulnerabilities in federated learning systems that arise from encrypted user payloads and changing identifiers, highlighting potential security risks in 5G networks.

articles.title: LLM-Driven AutoML for Cross-Lingual Handwritten OCR: Closed-Loop Neural Architecture Search with GPT-5, GPT-4o, and Claude Sonnet 4
articles.summary: A new AutoML framework leverages GPT-5, GPT-4o, and Claude Sonnet 4 to autonomously design neural architectures for cross-lingual handwritten optical character recognition. The system operates in a closed-loop manner, generating, training, and refining models based on performance feedback across Arabic, Persian, and English handwriting datasets.

articles.title: Think at 5 Hz, Act at 20 Hz: Asynchronous Fast-Slow Vision-Language-Action Inference for Closed-Loop Driving
articles.summary: Researchers have developed a fast-slow architecture for closed-loop driving that synchronizes large language model inference with vehicle control rates, allowing for more accurate and timely responses to environmental changes. This approach addresses the latency issues of existing models by enabling asynchronous processing, improving the effectiveness of driving agents.

articles.title: Orbis 2: A Hierarchical World Model for Driving
articles.summary: The article introduces Orbis 2, a hierarchical world model designed for driving that improves future prediction by operating at two distinct levels of abstraction and temporal scales. This model aims to enhance spatial reasoning and semantic understanding, addressing limitations of current single-level world models.

articles.title: LLM-Powered Agentic AI for 5G/6G Networks: A Tutorial and Survey on Architectures, Protocols, and Standardization
articles.summary: The article presents a tutorial and survey on the integration of Large Language Model-powered Agentic AI in 5G and 6G networks, highlighting the shift from rule-based automation to autonomous control. It aims to address gaps in existing literature regarding protocol integration, evaluation, and standardization in the context of Next-Generation Networks.

articles.title: Agents-K1: Towards Agent-native Knowledge Orchestration
articles.summary: The article introduces Agents-K1, a new end-to-end knowledge orchestration pipeline designed to enhance scientific reasoning by incorporating key entities, claims, evidence, mechanisms, and method lineages, which are often overlooked in current LLM-based research agents. This approach aims to improve the orchestration of scientific knowledge beyond the limitations of existing methods that primarily focus on abstracts and citations.

articles.title: 3D Motion Perception of Binocular Vision Target with PID-CNN
articles.summary: The article presents a trained neural network designed to perceive three-dimensional motion information from binocular vision targets, capable of providing real-time data on coordinates, velocity, and acceleration. It explores the application of PID control principles to enhance the network's ability to address nonlinear problems in spatiotemporal perception.
